subject: Hosting boundary evidence & private connectivity worksheet
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna.li@nutrisoft.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nutrisoft.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Regional hosting and private link evidence (NutriSoft)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're going through our security intake for a potential Private deployment of Redwood in the EU and have a few evidence requests so our security and procurement teams can sign off:

1) Confirmation that tenant data for a Private deployment (or Dedicated with private connectivity) will be hosted exclusively in an EU region (we prefer Frankfurt or Amsterdam).
2) Network connectivity options: do you support Azure Private Link and AWS PrivateLink / VPC peering? We need details on what endpoints exist and whether traffic leaves the customer's VNet.
3) KMS/key separation: can keys be customer-managed (BYOK) and can you confirm key material residency (EU-only) or HSM-backed key storage?
4) A short runbook for emergency data export/retention (how we would extract data if required by audit).
5) A high-level network diagram and any SOC2 or SIG artifacts you can share.

Can you send a checklist or worksheet we can use to track items internally? Procurement is looped on this email (procurement@nutrisoft.com) — if you can send artifacts and propose a 30–45m discovery slot this week or next, that would help us move quickly.

Thanks,
Anna Li
Information Security
NutriSoft

Attachments: none

Subject: Re: Regional hosting and private link evidence (NutriSoft)

Hi Anna —

Thanks for the clear list. I've put together a short worksheet and a few artifacts to address each ask; attaching the workbook and a network diagram plus our SOC2 summary to start. A few quick answers up front:

- Region: For Private deployments we can pin tenant compute and storage to EU regions (we commonly use eu-central-1 / Frankfurt). For Dedicated we can also guarantee capacity pinned to EU AZs.
- Connectivity: We support Azure Private Link, AWS PrivateLink, and provider peering. For Private deployments we typically establish a customer-managed Private Link endpoint so control stays in the customer VNet — traffic does not traverse public internet.
- KMS / Key separation: BYOK is supported. You can provision keys in your KMS (Azure Key Vault or AWS KMS) and we support key wrapping integrations; HSM-backed keys are supported where your KMS provides it. We can document options and the required IAM roles for the key usage.
- Runbook: I've included a short export runbook in the workbook and an outline in the network diagram PDF.

Attachments included (stubs):
- redwood_vpc_connection_workbook.xlsx (connection checklist + runbook + contact fields)
- network-diagram-eu.pdf (high-level private-link + routing + subnet boundaries)
- SOC2-summary.pdf (redacted SOC2 summary; full report available under NDA)

Next steps I propose:
1) Tell us which deployment mode you anticipate (Private vs Dedicated).
2) Complete the first tab in the workbook with your contact and preferred region.
3) Book a 45m discovery with our infra/security engineers (I can propose slots).

I've copied Ben (cc'd) for procurement coordination and Kimberly for technical handoff/validation. If you'd prefer, we can also put a short NDA in place before sharing unredacted paperwork.

Proposed discovery slots: Thu 8/27 10:00–10:45 BST or Mon 8/31 14:00–14:45 BST — let me know which works and I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Hi Anna —

Thanks — answers below inline to your questions and I've updated the workbook (see attachment reference).

> Can you confirm support for Azure Private Link specifically with Azure-hosted KMS and whether the Private Link integration keeps egress inside Azure's backbone?

Yes: we support Azure Private Link. For Private deployments we deploy a connector within your VNet that terminates on a private endpoint; control plane interactions for provisioning happen over the private channel and data plane traffic between your VNet and our compute nodes (if deployed in your VNet) remains on the cloud provider backbone — it does not traverse public internet. For Dedicated in a provider VPC, we use PrivateLink endpoints or VNet peering depending on provider; we document the specific endpoint hostnames in the workbook.

> Do we ever hold key material / can keys be exported by Redwood? HSM support?

We do not retain customer key material. For BYOK you provision keys in your KMS (Azure Key Vault or AWS KMS) and grant the runtime a constrained usage role (decrypt/sign) — Redwood never has export permissions for the key material. HSM-backed keys are supported where your KMS provides an HSM-backed key (e.g., Azure HSM-protected keys or AWS CloudHSM-backed keys). I've attached a short note on KMS partitioning and IAM roles and added a KMS details tab to the workbook. Attachment stub: kms-partitioning-note.md

Procurement tab: I've added the requested procurement checklist and DocuSign placeholders in the workbook. If procurement prefers, Ben will take the lead on the DocuSign envelope and timeline.

Next steps checklist:
- Please confirm desired deployment: Private (in your VNet) or Dedicated (Redwood-managed VPC with PrivateLink).
- Complete the contact & region fields on the first tab of the workbook.
- Ben will reach out to procurement to kick off DPA/contract timeline (cc'd).
- Schedule the 45m discovery so our infra/security engineers can validate the workbook answers and review the network diagram.

Proposed discovery: Mon 9/6 15:00–15:45 BST (Ben and Kimberly will join). If that works, I'll calendarize and include an agenda.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call earlier if you need anything sooner.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
